influential.comment: One commenter raised concern that notification of the proposal was not promptly circulated within industry and asked for an extension of the comment period.
influential.response: After reviewing the request, USDA published a notice reopening the comment period for an additional 30 days in the Federal Register on September 12, 2016.

influential.comment: One comment was received from Board staff indicating that the Board minutes stated the recommendation was for assessment allocation of $0.0065 per pound of tart cherries for promotion and $0.001 per pound of tart cherries for administration rather than the $0.006 and $0.0015, respectively, as published in the proposed rule.
influential.response: Accordingly, the allocation numbers were revised based on the comment received.

influential.comment: AMS received comments on the proposed rule for amending the annotation for parasiticides and the annotation for the specific parasiticides fenbendazole and moxidectin listed in Sec.  205.603.
influential.response: AMS agrees with the NOSB recommendation that the annotation for parasiticides be amended to clarify its use in organic livestock production.

influential.comment: AMS received comments that either supported or opposed adding propylene glycol to Sec.  205.603(a).
influential.response: AMS agrees with the NOSB recommendation that propylene glycol be allowed for use in organic livestock production.

influential.comment: AMS received comments on the proposed rule for amending sodium chlorite, acidified onto Sec.  205.603.
influential.response: AMS agrees with the NOSB recommendation that sodium chlorite, acidified be allowed for use in organic livestock production.

influential.comment: Based upon comments AMS received on amending zinc sulfate onto Sec.  205.603(a & b), zinc sulfate is added only to Sec.  205.603(b).
influential.response: AMS agrees with the NOSB recommendation that zinc sulfate be allowed for use in organic livestock production, adding it to Sec. 205.603(b).

influential.comment: Comments supporting the addition of hypochlorous acid to Sec. 205.601 from farmers, certifying agents, handlers, and commodity associations.
influential.response: AMS has considered the support and has added hypochlorous acid to Sec. 205.601.

influential.comment: Many comments from trade association groups, certifying agents, livestock producers and researcher supported the annotation amendment for methionine.
influential.response: AMS has considered the support and has made a determination on the amendment.

influential.comment: AMS received comments from industry groups and certifying agents indicating support for the reclassification of carnauba wax, although some received comments expressed opposition to all additions and amendments.
influential.response: AMS has considered the support and has reclassified carnauba wax.

influential.comment: Most of the comments received regarding the proposed addition of hypochlorous acid to Sec. 205.605 of the National List supported this addition.
influential.response: AMS has considered the support and has added hypochlorous acid to Sec. 205.605.

ignored.comment: One commenter argued that adding the phrase 'and coating material, if any is present' is unnecessary and could create unintended negative consequences.
One commenter opposed the definition of Acceptable test due to concerns about AOSA rules and tetrazolium testing.
One commenter supported label clarification but opposed including specific examples due to rapid product evolution.
Two commenters stated that biometric sampling may miss immature B. chilensis mites.
One commenter opposed adding a provision, arguing that VS should regulate waste and carcasses from animals infected with select agents to prevent spread.
Commenters requested clarification that biosafety and containment procedures should include animals outside the laboratory that may be exposed to select agents.
Commenter requested clarification on the definition of 'laboratory' and its scope.
Commenters argued that written risk assessments for each procedure are unnecessary and burdensome.
Commenters requested clarification on training levels for personnel with varying roles and access to select agents.
Commenter expressed concern about laboratory notebooks containing proprietary information and requested clarification on required information.
